lesson.title: Review Day: Getting to Know Washington State
lesson.subject: social-studies

contentBlocks.text: This week you learned real facts about Washington State. Let's review it all!

Quick review: Washington became the 42nd state in 1889 (Day 1). Its state bird, flower, and tree are official symbols (Day 2). Olympia is the capital, with a three-branch government (Day 3). Seattle grew large thanks to its Puget Sound location (Day 4). Answer: what year did Washington become a state, what is its capital, and name one state symbol.
Wonderful work this week — you learned real Washington State history, symbols, and government! Next week we'll explore something new.

objectives: Review Washington's statehood, symbols, capital/government, and major cities
Recall the statehood year, capital city, and one state symbol
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Do the quick walk-through review of all 4 days together, out loud.
2. Have the child answer all three review questions.
3. Complete the review worksheet.
4. Celebrate finishing a full week of real Washington State facts!
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus on just the capital and one symbol, the two most concrete/memorable facts from this week
Ready for more: ask the child to explain how this week's state-history content connects back to last week's geography content
This is a good checkpoint to note which of the week's facts needs the most reinforcement before the next Social Studies unit
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a recall and review activity — check that the child correctly states 1889, Olympia, and any one correct state symbol (American Goldfinch, Coast Rhododendron, or Western Hemlock).
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Consolidates this week's C3 Framework History and Civics content before the course continues, matching the established Day-5-review pacing used across every unit this session.
